fileTitle: Sabio x HP: Fewer PC Buyers, Paying More
footer: Proactive point of view for Zenith

slides.title: Fewer PC buyers, paying more. Find them first.
slides.subtitle: Consumer PC units are falling while prices rise. App Science® finds the households actually ready to buy a new PC this holiday, by the apps they use, and reaches them on the TV in the room.
slides.meta: Proactive recommendation | Prepared for Zenith | October 2026 | US only
slides.names:
Will Phung · Amanda Grond · Stamos Biliris
Ben Bring · Isabella Imbriano

stat.label: Consumer PC units, Q3 FY26
stat.body: Consumer Personal Systems revenue still grew 10% on price and mix. Each holiday buyer is worth more, and there are fewer of them. [1]

slides.title: What's happening at HP right now
slides.kicker: Four signals from the last eight months · Numbered sources on page 10

items.head: Record Q3 for Personal Systems at $11.77B
items.body: Total revenue grew 12.5% to $15.68B. Personal Systems grew 18.5%, a Q3 record, on pricing and a richer premium mix. [1]
items.means: Premium PCs are carrying the business. Media should sell premium.

items.head: AI PCs reached 46% of shipments
items.body: HP targets 50% by the end of fiscal 2026. Consumer units fell 19% while consumer revenue rose 10%. [1]
items.means: The AI PC story needs buyers who will use it. Apps show who they are.

items.head: Memory now 35% of what a PC costs to build
items.body: Up from 15% to 18% a quarter earlier. HP expected the PC market to shrink by double digits in 2026. [2]
items.means: Prices stay high this holiday, so wasted impressions cost more than usual.

items.head: Holiday e-commerce to grow 7.5% to 8.4%
items.body: Deloitte expects total holiday sales of $1.70T to $1.71T, up 4.0% to 4.8%. [3]
items.means: Buyers are out there, but HP has to win them earlier and more precisely.

slides.title: The opening: find the ready buyer
slides.kicker: Why HP's holiday media should chase intent, not age and income
slides.statLabel: Share of US TV time spent on streaming in July 2026. Broadcast was 19.5%.
slides.headline: We think HP's holiday is won by reaching the homes whose apps show they need more computer, not the homes that fit a demo.

points.head: The apps show the need
points.body: Video editing, design, PC gaming and school apps are heavy workloads. A home running them is closer to an upgrade.

points.head: The rivals show the shopping
points.body: Dell, Lenovo and Best Buy apps opened this month mean someone is comparing. That's a home to win now.

points.head: The TV starts the gift
points.body: Half of TV time is streaming. We put HP there, then follow the same home to the phone and the retailer.

slides.title: Three audiences for the holiday PC buyer
slides.kicker: Each one is an app ecosystem, not a demographic · Sized on the final build
slides.source: HP's own apps (HP Smart, OMEN Gaming Hub) can be used to reinforce owners or suppress them for net-new reach. App lists finalized with HP and Zenith.

cards.desc: Edits video, designs and studies on a laptop. Feels the limits of an older machine.

cards.name: The PC gamer

cards.apps: Steam · Discord · Xbox · NVIDIA app · Twitch

slides.side:
HP is selling fewer PCs at higher prices, and holiday is when consumers buy.

We think the answer is fewer, better impressions, aimed at homes whose apps show they need a new machine.

That said, product focus matters here. We'd want to know which lines lead before we size anything.
